arguments.summary: A credential compromise incident initiated from external IP 91.219.236.174 led to lateral movement and potential credential harvesting within the Finance department. The initial access vector was an Nmap scan detected on 2026-04-08, followed by successful authentication from a compromised internal host. Although the EDR showed no suspicious activity on the primary endpoint (10.0.10.51), a webshell ('Webshell.PHP.Generic.A') was discovered during post-incident scanning. Immediate credential revocation was attempted but denied by policy controls, indicating a gap in automated response authorization. The attacker likely exploited cached credentials, necessitating a broad credential reset strategy.

timeline.description: External IP 91.219.236.174 conducts Nmap SYN scan against internal asset 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101). Logged by IDS.
Successful authentication from 10.0.2.15 to domain controller (10.0.1.1) as CORP\helpdesk. Potential lateral movement.
Incident initiated: Compromised account j.martinez identified with source IP 10.0.10.51.
EDR query on 10.0.10.51 shows normal user activity (explorer.exe, chrome.exe), no immediate anomalies.
SIEM confirms 23 failed authentication attempts for j.martinez in the last 24 hours from multiple sources.
Sandbox analysis of file hash 3c009b0e returns 'clean' verdict with low risk score, but behavioral note on standard API usage.
EPP/AV full scan on 10.0.10.51 detects and quarantines webshell: Webshell.PHP.Generic.A at /var/www/html/.shell.php.
Attempt to revoke j.martinez and related accounts via IAM/PAM tool fails due to lack of approval workflow integration.
